newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice announces indictment in ADM probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice announces indictment in ADM probe.

text.p: A federal grand jury in Chicago Tuesday indicted three former top Archer Daniels Midland Co. executives for conspiring to fix lysine prices, the Justice Department said.

It said the indictment named Michael Andreas, the former executive vice president and son of ADM's chairman; former Vice President Terrance Wilson, who headed up the corn-processing unit; and Mark Whitacre, a fired ADM executive who had been an FBI informant in the case.

The Justice Department also announced that Cheil Jedang Ltd., based in Seoul, South Korea, agreed to plead guilty and pay a $1.25 million fine for participating in the conspiracy to fix prices of lysine, a feed additive for livestock.

Apart from the three former ADM executives, the Justice Department said the grand jury also indicted Kazutoshi Yamada, a managing director of Ajinomoto Co. Inc. The Japanese company previously entered a guilty plea in the investigation.

In October, Archer Daniels Midland agreed to plead guilty to two counts of federal charges of price fixing in the sale of agricultural products and to pay record fines totalling $100 million. The indictment of ADM's former executives had been expected since then.
The Justice Department said its antitrust investigation into the lysine, citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup markets continues.
